title: Cornmeal Skillet Sally Lunn
description: A lightly sweet, cornmeal-flecked yeast batter bakes into a tender round loaf.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Combine {ap}, {cornmeal}, {milk}, {egg}, {butter}, {honey}, {yeast}, {salt}. Use room-temperature liquids and softened fat. Mix until no dry flour remains.

steps.title: Develop the dough
steps.text: Beat the batter with a sturdy spoon for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Let rise
steps.text: Cover and let rise 45–75 minutes at room temperature until about doubled.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Scrape the thick batter into a greased 8-inch metal pan or 8-inch oven-safe skillet; level the top.

steps.title: Proof
steps.text: Cover and proof 30–50 minutes until puffy; a light fingertip dent should return slowly.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the Samsung oven to 375°F on conventional Bake.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake until the dome springs back and the crumb is set. Allow 27–32 minutes; verify 190°F at the center.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool on a rack for 60 minutes before slicing.

notes: Make ahead: weigh the dry ingredients the evening before. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Cool completely and freeze sliced or individually wrapped for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: wrap a serving in a damp towel and microwave for 15–25 seconds. Freezer reheat: thaw wrapped, then warm the same way. Serve with soup or gravy for a softer bite. Allow about 1–2 hours for rising and proofing in addition to mixing and baking. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/8 of recipe): 161 kcal, 5.6 g protein, 27.2 g total carbohydrate, 3.3 g fat, 1.4 g fiber, 168 mg sodium.
